name: Ideology
scope: Ideology here is the concept and the study of ideology: a system of ideas, values or beliefs held by a person or group and bearing on how society works or should work, from Destutt de Tracy's coinage of the 'science of ideas' (1796) through the Marxist account of ideology as ideas shaped by class position, Mannheim's sociology of knowledge, Gramsci's hegemony and Althusser's interpellation. The defining sources (the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry, Britannica, Mannheim's Ideology and Utopia and Ricoeur's Lectures on Ideology and Utopia) treat it as a general phenomenon and a contested concept, covering the neutral descriptive sense (political belief systems), the critical sense (distortion that serves power) and the epistemological sense. The scope is the concept itself, not any single political ideology (liberalism, Marxism or fascism are separate subjects) and not books that only use the word for another subject (the Sumerian royal ideology, anti-communism, ISIS), which are left out as coatracks. Marx and Engels's The German Ideology is a key work because the sources treat it as the foundation of the critical concept; Marx, Gramsci and Althusser are key figures of Marxism and Western Marxism, which reserve them, so only their texts are tied here.

keyFigures.role: Coined 'ideology' in 1796 as the science of ideas
keyFigures.quote: it was introduced by a philosopher, A.-L.-C. Destutt de Tracy

keyFigures.role: Sociologist of knowledge; theorist of the particular and total conceptions of ideology

summary: Ideology is the general concept, and the study, of systems of ideas, values and beliefs held by a person or group, from Destutt de Tracy's 1796 'science of ideas' to the Marxist critique of ideas as shaped by the ruling class and Mannheim's sociology of knowledge. The defining sources describe the phenomenon and its contested senses (neutral, critical and epistemological) rather than advocating a programme for society, so the test's statements are mostly unanswered; the one it settles is that the ideas dominant in a society reflect the interests of its ruling class.

notes: Scope is the concept of ideology (PROMPT.md sections 1-2): the Stanford Encyclopedia, Britannica, Mannheim's Ideology and Utopia, Ricoeur's lectures and the ideology theory of The German Ideology. Searched the statements for ideology, knowledge, ruling class, media, propaganda, education and pragmatism topics. The other local books (Destutt de Tracy's Treatise on Political Economy, Mannheim's Freedom, Power and Democratic Planning and the Spanish and German Mannheim editions) hold their authors' own programmes (free-market economics, democratic planning, communism in The German Ideology outside its theory of ideology); the defining sources do not tie these to the concept, so they answer nothing here. Books using the word for another subject (Sumerian royal ideology, anti-communism, ISIS, Nehru, Brownson, the travel and campaign books) are coatracks and not cited. Wikipedia-redirect aliases are listed as in the scope phase.
